newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African T-bill rate seen little changed.
newsitem.headline: South African T-bill rate seen little changed.

text.p: The average rate for South African three-month Treasury bills at Friday's auction is likely to be little changed from last week's 14.93 percent, despite a sharp rise in money market rates this week, dealers said.
"We may see the rate rise, but not much -- perhaps to around 14.97 or 14.98. There still is a big squeeze on liquid assets," one money market dealer said.
In addition, the Reserve Bank was still keeping a tight rein on supply with the offer in the three-month area limited to 700 million rand, other traders noted.
Little immediate relief is seen in banks' need for liquid assets with the daily money market shortage nudging 10 bilion rand -- exceptionally high for mid-month.
The money market shortage rose to 9.823 billion on Thursday from 9.677 billion on Wednesday.
As a result the current big differential between the T-bill rate and Bankers Acceptance (BA) rates was likely to continue.
Banks were quoting the 90-day BA rate at 16.30 to 16.75 percent on Friday, a huge premium over the anticipated T-bill rate. The differential is usuaully under 25 b.p.
The BA rate was between 16.10 and 16.25 percent last Friday.
One trader said banks would get some relief when one third of the 24 billion rand of R147 stock qualified for liquid asset status at the beginning of December.
But this would be offset by some 6.5 billion rand of R146s maturing.
"We've got 6-1/2 (billion rand) maturing and something over 7-1/2 coming in -- it will help, but not that much," the trader said.
Results of the weekly T-bill tender are due around 1000 GMT.
